Variant 1 — Syntactical Proof Assistant (`variants/variant1_first_order/`, 1st-Order with `ProofOf`)
Built on a 1st-order NBG/MK core (newchecker.ML, types/typetheory.ML, types/foundations.ML) where formulas (Fm), contexts (Ctx), theories (Theory), statements (Stmt), and proofs (Prf) are explicit syntax-tree datatypes (⟨...⟩ / ⟦...⟧). Because statements are syntactic objects, theoremhood requires ProofOf / ProofsOf ((p : ProofOf(s)) and (Enc(p) ∈ ProofsOf(Enc(s)))).
Syntactic Implication (→): In Variant 1, ((φ → ψ) : Fm) is the syntactic propositional connective between formula ASTs (defined as (¬φ ∨ ψ)), distinct from the semantic class of functions (A → B) in Variant 2 (see dual meaning of →).
NBG vs. Morse–Kelley (MK) Comprehension (3.01): Schema 3.01 (comprehension) is parameterized in foundations.ML by check_flag : bool: with check_flag = false it provides full impredicative Morse–Kelley (MK) class comprehension (bound variables may range over arbitrary classes), whereas setting check_flag = true (or restricting class formation to the finite Bernays–Gödel algebraic operators 3.02–3.35) yields conservative 1st-order NBG (predicative comprehension over sets (x ∈ V) only).

2.01 Axiom Discourse domain is non-empty
Typing Judgments: \(({\color{#f87171}{K}} : {\color{#22d3ee}{\mathsf{Class}}})\)\({\color{#f87171}{K}} : {\color{#22d3ee}{\mathsf{Class}}}\)
⚡ SML Kernel AST: program/types/foundations.ML (2.01: Discourse domain is non-empty) :: Discourse domain is non-empty
(∃([K@Variable]:[Class@Type]) ⊤)
▸ Note
Layered axiomatization: Section 2 axiomatizes pure First-Order Predicate Logic over sort Class prior to Section 3 (Class Comprehension). In multi-sorted / inclusive predicate logic (where some sorts like Nonstored / Void are uninhabited), 2.01 explicitly postulates that the sort Class is inhabited so (∀(K : Class) φ) → (∃(K : Class) φ) holds in pure predicate logic; once Section 3's Class Comprehension Axiom (3.01) is added, 2.01 becomes derivable (witnessed by ∅).

3.01 Axiom Class Comprehension Axiom
Symbol Signature: (∈: (Class × Class → Bool))((∈) :: ((Class × Class) → Bool))  |  (∉: (Class × Class → Bool))((∉) :: ((Class × Class) → Bool))
⚡ SML Kernel AST: program/types/foundations.ML (3.01: Class comprehension) :: Class comprehension
(([⦃[x@Variable.Expression]⦄@Class.Expression] ∈ { [⦃[x@Variable.Expression]⦄@Class.Expression] | ⟦[φ@Fm.Expression]⟧ }) ⟷ (([⦃[x@Variable.Expression]⦄@Class.Expression] set) ∧ ⟦[φ@Fm.Expression]⟧))
▸ Note
In Variant 1 (1st-Order NBG/MK), Class Comprehension is formalized at the metalevel as an axiom schema (class_comprehension_rul / class_comprehension_meta_axm_fm in foundations.ML, entry 4.06) parameterized by an arbitrary formula expression φ : Fm with side condition NFV(v_C, φ). In full Morse–Kelley (MK), φ may contain bound class variables (impredicative comprehension); in pure NBG, φ is predicative (quantifies only over sets) and is finitely axiomatizable via Bernays–Gödel class-existence axioms B1–B7. Lowercase x, y are used by naming convention because elements of classes must be sets (isSet(x)).

Dependent conditional constructor if_dep (displayed as if_{dep}) quantified at the metalevel over syntactic type-family expressions T_e : (Bool → Type_Expression). For boolean condition b : Bool and branches t₁ : ⟦T_e(true)⟧, t₂ : ⟦T_e(false)⟧, if_dep(b, t₁, t₂) has dependent type ⟦T_e(b)⟧ and reduces to t₁ on true and t₂ on false.

3.32 Theorem Ordinal / Transitive-Class ∈-Induction (∈-Ind)
Symbol Signature: (On: Class)(On :: Class)
⚡ SML Kernel AST: program/types/foundations.ML (3.71: General form of the induction principle on a transitive class) :: General form of the induction principle on a transitive class
(∀([K@Variable]:[Class@Type])∀([A@Variable]:[Class@Type]) ((Tr([K@Class.Expression]) ∧ (([K@Class.Expression] ∩ 𝒫([A@Class.Expression])) ⊆ [A@Class.Expression])) → ([K@Class.Expression] ⊆ [A@Class.Expression])))
▸ Note
Transfinite ∈-induction in both its first-order class form ∀(K, A : Class) ((Tr(K) ∧ ((K ∩ 𝒫(A)) ⊆ A)) → (K ⊆ A)) (exported from the SML kernel as epsilon_induction_thm, SML ID 3.71: for any transitive class K—in particular K = On—if every element of K whose members lie in A also lies in A, then K ⊆ A) and its schematic formula form over A = {x ∈ On | φ(x)} (PEpsIndAx_prf in newchecker.ML, with syntactic side condition Fresh(v_y, v_x) ∧ NFV(v_y, φ(x))). Derived in Morse–Kelley from the Regularity / Foundation Axiom (3.12 / SML ID 3.14).

Foundations ch. 110 (Semi-Singleton Subset, sss_def_entry, 3.36 in foundations.ML): binary infix relation (s sss A) asserting that s is a subclass of A with at most one element: (s ⊆ A) ∧ semi_singleton(s). For any class A (whether a set or a proper class), the sets s satisfying (s sss A) are ∅ and {a} for each element a ∈ A; hence their unary union reconstructs A itself: ⋃{ s | s sss A } = A (Theorem 110.1 in 110_family_evaluation.tex). By contrast, extracting the unique element a from a singleton class X = {a} uses unary intersection: Value(X) = ⋂{ y ∈ X | semi_singleton(X) } (Foundations 040_old_variant_of_iota_defs.tex §614 & 190_union_intersection.tex §65), so Value({a}) = ⋂{a} = a whereas Value(∅) = Value({a, b}) = ⋂∅ = V (proper class / nonset).

Foundations ch. 130 (Classes as Types — Dependent Product Π, lines 949–1086 of 130_classes_as_types.tex): provides two complementary models depending on whether the domain A = Dom(B) is a proper class or a set. (1) Model 1 — Conglomerate / Typing Predicate (f : ΠB) (general class domain Dom(B), pi_predicate_model_def_entry, 3.39 in foundations.ML): when Dom(B) is a proper class (such as V or On), a section f with Dom(f) = Dom(B) is itself a proper class and cannot be an element of a class comprehension { f | ... }; instead, (f : ΠB) is defined directly as the first-order predicate isFamily(f) ∧ (Dom(f) = Dom(B)) ∧ ∀(x ∈ Dom(B)) (f(x) ∈ B(x)). (2) Model 2 — Class of Set Sections ΠB (when isSet(Dom(B)) holds): when the domain A = Dom(B) is a set, every section f ⊆ ΣB with Dom(f) = A is a set (by Replacement and Union), so the class comprehension ΠB = { f ∈ 𝒫(ΣB) | isFunction(f) ∧ (Dom(f) = Dom(B)) ∧ ∀(x ∈ Dom(B)) (f(x) ∈ B(x)) } collects all dependent functions.
